questions.question: Two mirrors, one concave (f₁ = 20 cm) and one convex (f₂ = -15 cm), are placed facing each other 50 cm apart. An object is placed 30 cm in front of the concave mirror. The position of the final image formed after two reflections (first by concave, then by convex) is:

options.explanation: The final image is formed in front of the convex mirror.

options.text: 12 cm in front of the convex mirror
options.explanation: The final image is formed in front of the convex mirror.
The final image is formed in front of the convex mirror.

options.text: 25 cm in front of the convex mirror
options.explanation: The final image is formed in front of the convex mirror, but the correct distance is approximately 24.78 cm.

questions.explanation: Step 1: Image by concave mirror (f₁ = 20 cm, u = -30 cm): 1/f₁ = 1/v₁ + 1/u → 1/20 = 1/v₁ - 1/30 → 1/v₁ = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12 → v₁ = 12 cm (real image in front of the concave mirror). Step 2: This image acts as an object for the convex mirror (f₂ = -15 cm). Distance between mirrors = 50 cm. Object distance for convex mirror: u₂ = -(50 - 12) = -38 cm. 1/f₂ = 1/v₂ + 1/u₂ → -1/15 = 1/v₂ - 1/38 → 1/v₂ = 1/38 - 1/15 = (15 - 38)/(570) = -23/570 → v₂ ≈ -24.78 cm.
